# SelfSentry measured full-pipeline evaluation — 11 October 2026

## Evidence and configuration

Source: `selfsentry-full-evidence.tar.gz`, containing the 200 records in
`state/evaluation/full-20261011-only.jsonl`, their schedule, incident snapshot,
aggregated results, and the 20-sample target baseline.
All 200 trial IDs and schedule entries are unique; all records share configuration
fingerprint `961602fe18bdd46c05d5260cc19df8234fe789f9b1ff464f0656f41b9a0b65a9`.
The uploaded baseline SHA-256 matches the recorded fingerprint:
`f354809d2ad5fa7406e34024bb65c9f3aea37815493050b92741debac412fbba`.
Target: container `12160024642b`; 60-second windows, 10-second lateness;
automatic isolation off. No invalid trials or duplicate-incident trials were recorded.
The software working tree was dirty: the fingerprint does not establish identical
runtime code across future runs. Preserve the actual source used for this experiment.

## Measured outcomes

| Scenario | Labeled trials | Persisted incident | Qualifying ML evidence in persisted incidents | Auto-confirmed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Terminal shell | 20 attack | 20 | 1 | 0 |
| New binary execution | 20 attack | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| Sensitive file read | 20 attack | 20 | 2 | 2 |
| Symlink over sensitive file | 20 attack | 20 | 3 | 3 |
| Standard stream/socket redirection | 20 attack | 20 | 1 | 0 |
| Benign administration | 20 benign | 0 | 0 (retrospective replay) | 0 |
| Benign configuration read | 10 benign | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Benign local HTTP fixture | 10 benign | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| Benign shell directory listing | 20 benign | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Quiet | 40 benign | 0 | Not scored: no events | 0 |

Incident detection: 100/100 attacks (Wilson 95% interval 96.30–100%).
False-positive rate: 13/100 benign trials (7.76–20.98%). Forty benign trials
were quiet; among the 60 active benign trials, incidents occurred in 13/60 (21.67%).
Attack automatic-confirmation coverage: 5/100 (2.15–11.18%).
Confirmation precision under the controlled scenario labels: 5/5 (56.55–100%).
Controlled simulations are labels for this experiment, not evidence of genuine compromise.

All 100 attack incidents contain Falco security alerts. Only seven have qualifying
ML evidence; five meet automatic-confirmation policy. The evidence does not establish
an attack-detection advantage over Falco, nor an independently operated Falco-only trial.
The subsequent retrospective comparison covers all 200 windows and is recorded below.
Do not populate unrun live comparison variants by copying full-pipeline results into them.

## Timing boundary

Attack start to database row timestamp: median 68.154 seconds; nearest-rank p95
68.588 seconds; maximum 69.279 seconds, n=100. Naive database timestamps were explicitly
interpreted as Asia/Kolkata and converted to UTC. These server-generated row timestamps
are not verified transaction-commit completion timestamps. This scheduled run did not
poll incident visibility, or measure Falco receipt, ML qualification, correlation,
isolation, learning, or model readiness latencies. Those measurements remain unavailable.

## False-positive attribution

The ten benign HTTP incidents contain `Redirect STDOUT/STDIN to Network Connection in
Container`, two alert entries per incident. Their ML score is approximately 0.4582 and
does not qualify. The benign fixture uses Bash `/dev/tcp` plus redirected streams to
make a loopback HTTP request: it performs the operation this rule monitors. Preserve
these ten known-benign detections. A conventional HTTP-client fixture would constitute
a separate workload/configuration comparison; do not retrospectively relabel the trials,
exclude them, or disable the general socket-redirection security rule to remove this result.

The two configuration-read false positives are anomaly-only (score approximately 0.8430),
as is the directory-listing false positive (approximately 0.8455). None was confirmed.
No global threshold change can be justified solely from these individual examples.

## Workflow and AI evidence

Of 113 persisted incidents: 108 unconfirmed, five confirmed; all 113 responses are
not attempted because isolation is off. Five candidates are pending human review:
rule IDs 12–16 from incidents 70, 80, 94, 98 and 151. These are not deployment evidence;
their backtests and native validation need review before approval.
AI explanations: 50 ready, 63 unavailable. The operator's run-scoped JSON log
count reported 50 HTTP 200 responses, 63 HTTP 429 responses and 63 unavailable
warnings, with no unparseable log lines. This attributes the failures to provider
rate limiting; the specific request/token/quota limit was not established. AI
availability is not a detection/confirmation criterion. A bounded retry patch was installed afterward and the full test suite passed on the VM.
A post-patch request for incident 177 succeeded with HTTP 200. Live 429-to-success
recovery was not observed; cooldown, retry limits and restart persistence have
automated-test coverage.

## Acceptance and review closeout

No-baseline live fallback (incident 178), PostgreSQL outage recovery (179), and
real-Docker protected-container workflow checks (name/short/full ID) passed.
Five invalid/degenerate-model regression cases passed. All three acceptance
summaries were reviewed from the source archive. Protection used synthetic policy
evidence and a fake backend; the other two checks used the actual running pipeline.
A local review reproduced 406 Python test passes. Final polish requires a final VM
verification and release commit; it does not reclassify or replace the frozen trials.

Independent live comparison variants and separate layer/response/learning timings
remain unmeasured. Exhaustive fault injection and production soak remain limitations.
Human review of outstanding candidates remains an operator workflow, not a requirement
to deploy every generated rule. Old whoami-from-sh rule 32 is still enabled and broad;
review it before using automation on real workloads. The prior ls-from-sh rule 8 is disabled.

## Verified retrospective layer comparison

Local replay on the test VM verified all 113 saved incident assessments against
retained telemetry and the matching baseline. All 200 reconstructed union outcomes
matched persisted incident outcomes (zero mismatches).

| Layer observation | Attack flags / 100 | Benign flags / 100 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Stored Falco security alerts | 100 | 10 |
| Replayed ML qualification (threshold 0.8) | 7 | 3 |
| Union / persisted full-pipeline incidents | 100 | 13 |
| Automatic confirmation | 5 | 0 |

ML scored all 100 attack and 60 active benign windows. Forty quiet windows contained
no baseline telemetry and were not scored: absence of ML qualification there is not
an affirmative normal classification. Among scored benign windows, ML qualified 3/60.
The union of Falco and ML flags added three false positives and no additional attack
detections for these scenarios. This is an observation/replay comparison from one
full-pipeline execution, not four independently executed experimental variants.
Live Falco receipt and ML processing latencies remain unmeasured.

## Post-patch verification — 11 October UTC / 12 October IST

The operator reported the full Python suite passing after installing the AI retry
patch and updating obsolete evaluation-contract tests. The exact final pass count
was not pasted. Monitor PID 41437 restarted healthy; the existing target remained
MODEL_READY with 20 samples. Incident 177 was detected and auto-confirmed with no
duplicate incident, clock skew zero, and trial-start-to-API-visibility duration
70.0758 seconds. Its AI explanation became ready (HTTP 200); automatic isolation
was not attempted because it was disabled. This is a separate smoke test, not an
additional observation in the frozen 200-trial comparison.

AI wording that calls this controlled simulation a compromised container is an
advisory overstatement. The ground-truth scenario label remains a controlled test.

# Designed-case coverage matrix

> Current status: [21 October academic handoff](academic_handoff_20261021.md). It records the latest rule workflow, benign false positive and clock recurrence. Historical entries below retain their original scope.


SelfSentry is a hybrid container runtime security system that combines Falco rule matching with per-container behavioral anomaly detection, correlates both into incidents, and converts confirmed anomalies into template-generated, backtested, human-approved Falco rules — demonstrating a supervised adaptive detection loop under controlled evaluation.

15 October 2026. **PASS-E**: supplied study artifacts checked offline; **PASS-H**:
earlier reported live pass; **TEST**: source test; **RE-RUN**: evidence still needed.
PASS-E does not mean the reviewer independently operated the VM.
The 15 October study exercised Falco-backed process metadata. The 16 October
extension supports proposals with a retained literal syscall witness; aggregate-only
anomalies remain unsupported. The new anomaly-only live chain remains unverified.

| Case | Expected behavior | Evidence / next artifact | Pass–Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Falco-only high priority | Persist alert without invented agreement | Binary incidents 200/204: Critical stock alert, IF ~0.143 nonqualifying, responses off | PASS-E |
| No baseline / learning | Falco incident, explicit unavailable ML | Incident 178; shell probe `reliability-shell-20261012T174808Z.json` | PASS-H |
| Both layers agree | Falco + qualifying default IF assessment | Seven frozen attack windows; IF incident 177 | PASS-H; refresh current case |
| Confirm → candidate | Persist confirmation; template; nonempty backtest; pending queue | 209 confirmed by guna; candidates 21 and 22; 0/65 corpus matches | Operator-supplied current functional pass |
| Anomaly-only synthesis | Retain qualifying same-container/window literal witness; refuse aggregate-only input; require backtest and human approval | Benign incident 211: IF 0.821809; no security alert; literal file witness | Detection/witness observed; synthesis/deployment/re-fire unverified |
| Reject → undeployed | Reviewer saved; exact candidate absent; reason audited | Rule 21 rejected, reason/reviewer retained in audit 949; absent at check | Operator-supplied current functional pass |
| Approve → reload → re-fire | Human decision + active native rule | Rule 22 approved/deployed, audits 951–953; native match linked 210 via 954 | Operator-supplied current functional pass; refreshed timeline confirmed |
| Monitor restart | Resume durable work without duplicate/timeline loss | [Reviewed graceful restart during DB outage](live_restart_results_20261021.md): pending key retained, incident 208, unchanged timeline, one row in bounded duplicate query | PASS-E for this case; crash/other fault extensions NOT RUN |
| Backend/DB restart recovery | Queue drains to one incident after recovery | Incident 179 PostgreSQL outage in `monitor_final_review.md` | PASS-H for recorded outage |
| Isolation default OFF | Standard study makes no response attempt | All 17 capture flags false; six incident responses not attempted | PASS-E for study |
| Clock skew | Reject skew; retain invalid evidence | One reboot/resume check passed; later ~67.5s and ~16437.6s skew recurred | Clock guard observed; permanent correction OPEN |
| Broad template preview | Flag unsafe corpus match rate | 201: 3/36; 202: 8/36; not submitted; no actual refusal calls | PASS-E preview; submission unrun |
| Later benign windows | No learned-rule hits in new windows | Historical 0/3 learned-rule hit windows separate; current pilot has incident 211 in 1/6 benign windows | Pilot complete; representative longer validation OPEN |
| Experimental response | Eligible SVM/Falco isolation + recoverable resume | Incident 190, saved JSON + paused-state console; acceptance doc | PASS-H, SVM-only functional case |

Evidence index: [measured results](monitor_measured_results_20261011.md),
[acceptance](reliability_acceptance_20261013.md), [protocol](academic_study.md),
[reviewed study](academic_results_20261015.md).
Mark actual FAIL, INVALID or NOT RUN where appropriate after execution; preserve IDs,
artifact paths, exclusions and configuration hashes. Never infer a pass from a proposed command.

**Out of scope:** universal/zero-day coverage; production CWPP/fleets/Kubernetes/
multi-tenancy; autonomous rule deployment; model self-retraining; ML-only pattern
invention; representative production FPR; unrun independent live ablations;
complete stage/containment latency; exhaustive failure/soak validation. Backtesting
estimates corpus matches, not safety; templates can lose original context.

# Supervised adaptive-loop results — 15 October 2026

SelfSentry is a hybrid container runtime security system that combines Falco rule matching with per-container behavioral anomaly detection, correlates both into incidents, and converts confirmed anomalies into template-generated, backtested, human-approved Falco rules — demonstrating a supervised adaptive detection loop under controlled evaluation.

**Observed boundary:** this study validates the supported Falco-backed process-pattern
workflow. It does not establish ML-only rule synthesis, added attack coverage or
representative model accuracy. “Confirmed” denotes operator-labeled controlled
simulation, not a genuine compromise. No detector default or threshold was changed.

## Evidence and review method

The operator executed the study on the Ubuntu/Docker/Falco/PostgreSQL VM and supplied
`selfsentry-academic-study-evidence.tar.gz`. The review extracted and checked those
artifacts offline; the reviewer did not operate the VM independently. Archive SHA-256:

```text
0fa955f30775b8c1edbc2638d87d334091e95c56f1311523024dc0e912383981
```

Study directory: `state/evaluation/academic-loop-20261015T085928Z/`.
See the [machine-readable audit](academic_results_20261015.json) for each capture,
backtest, reviewed row, artifact hash and unmeasured item. Raw runtime data remains
separate from tracked source documentation.

Seventeen captures are present: nine benign calibration windows, three primary before
cases, one additional binary rejection-control before case, one approved binary after
case, and three later benign windows. All 17 reports are valid with closed windows,
accepted baseline telemetry and zero observed per-capture clock skew. Raw record
counts, target/window membership, alert names, incident IDs, delivered outbox IDs and
persisted timeline descriptions were cross-checked. No invalid capture is present in
this supplied archive; this says nothing about attempts not supplied.

All captures used monitor PID 10064, default `isolation_forest` and explicit false
values for isolation, automatic confirmation and automatic candidate generation. The
same target, image and baseline hashes were recorded throughout. Six incident snapshots
(199–204) all report response not attempted because isolation was disabled. Manual
confirmation/submission and human rule approval were separate operator actions.

| Reproducibility item | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Source HEAD | `f465de1930df502c3ea4b426f0804a47298a2e72` with dirty working tree and applied academic patch |
| Container ID | `12160024642b6244d4ec9b81e5ac7d0010a8d30688e37d9ac4369f0bf2b693df` |

| Generated rules before | `59874ffbd84bad5c80c8a75271d1425d58a4ce3c260e6800fb06867097e601d6` |
| Generated rules after | `99ad05160795da3d62787cbd39af3d648821cd2385a21f43f5f5eabcce3425a4` |

The archive has captures and final rule/decision snapshots; it does not contain a
complete runtime source/configuration/dependency archive, original baseline bytes,
native reload journal or full DB audit export. Source HEAD plus dirty status is not
proof of exact runtime-code identity. Stored model assessments were inspected, not
retrained/recomputed from a baseline absent from this archive.

## Novelty evidence table: all planned primary behaviors and rejection control

| Behavior | Falco before | Incident confirmed | Rule approved | Falco after (re-fire?) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 copied harmless `ss-study-true` binary | Existing `Drop and execute new binary in container`; incident 200 | Yes: reviewed record links incident 200, confirmed by `guna-academic-review` | Yes: rule 18, reviewed by `guna-review`, final status deployed | **Yes:** exact `Auto_Generated_ss_study_true_from_sh_200` at `2026-10-15T10:12:02.312672440Z`, incident 204 timeline | Candidate matched 0/36 benign process events; stock alert also fires after; no coverage gain |
| B2 sensitive-file read | Existing `Read sensitive file untrusted`; incident 201 | No confirmation evidence supplied for this case | Not submitted/approved; preview backtest fails | NOT RUN; no B2 generated rule in final YAML | `cat` from `sh` matches 3/36 (8.33%); template loses sensitive-path context |
| B3 terminal shell | Existing `Terminal shell in container`; incident 202 | No confirmation evidence supplied for this case | Not submitted/approved; preview backtest fails | NOT RUN; no B3 generated rule in final YAML | `sh` from `containerd-shim` matches 8/36 (22.22%); template loses TTY context |
| Rejection control: additional B1 repeat | Existing copied-binary rule; incident 203 | Yes: reviewed record links incident 203, confirmed by `guna-academic-review` | **Explicitly rejected:** rule 19 by `guna-review` | Exact `_203` rule absent from final YAML and every supplied capture; positive after run fires `_200` only | Separate decision-path control, not a fourth attack class; same matching condition as rule 18 |

Exactly one of the three primary behaviors completed approval and native re-fire.
Two primary patterns stopped at failed backtest previews. An additional passing
candidate was explicitly rejected. These are different outcomes: **a backtest preview
failure is not a recorded human rejection**, and neither missing B2/B3 after-run is
counted as a successful re-fire. Actual failed production submissions for 201/202
were not attempted; source refusal behavior has test coverage, not live refusal
trace in this study.

## Backtest corpus and recomputation

The corpus contains 36 `Baseline Process Spawn` records from nine known-normal
administration/config-read/conventional-curl windows (three rounds). Offline review
reconstructed that exact ordered corpus from the raw capture files and matched its
saved hash. It retained the normal window that produced anomaly-only incident 199.
The corpus is separate from the model's unchanged training baseline.

| Pattern preview from actual incident | Matched / eligible events | Reported match rate | Verdict at existing ≤5% threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `ss-study-true` from `sh` (200) | 0/36 | 0.0% | Pass; queued rule 18 |
| `cat` from `sh` (201) | 3/36 | 8.33% | Flag for revision; not queued |
| `sh` from `containerd-shim` (202) | 8/36 | 22.22% | Flag for revision; not queued |

Existing `extract_pattern`, `generate_rule` and `backtest_rule` reproduced all three
reported previews against the saved corpus. Submission artifacts and reviewed rows
agree for rules 18/19. Backtest rates are event-level matches over the supported
process/parent template shape, not native full-engine replay or production FPR.
Zero matches in 36 events is not a safety guarantee. Across-container rule breadth
and loss of incident-specific context still require human review.

## Human decisions, native deployment evidence and rejection integrity

`reviewed-rules.json` records rule 18 from incident 200 as deployed, and rule 19 from
incident 203 as rejected. Both were confirmed by `guna-academic-review` and reviewed
by `guna-review`. The final rule-18 YAML equals the corresponding parsed node in
`rules-after.yaml`; rule 19 is absent. Reviewer timestamps are timezone-naive in the
export; no learning or approval latency is calculated from them.

The intermediate `rejection-verification.json` records rule 19 rejected/absent,
the file hash unchanged and rule 18 still pending. The control's before capture
shares the original rule hash. Together these support the rejection outcome; they
are operator-generated snapshots, not an independently signed audit trail. The full
rejection-reason/audit event payload is not included in this archive.

The after raw record contains the exact rule name, target `12160024642b`, process
`ss-study-true`, parent `sh` and native timestamp above. The stock copied-binary rule
has the **same event timestamp**. Incident 204's observed timeline contains both
alerts. Thus the rule was active in Falco after the operator's reported reload;
this goes beyond a database status alone. A separate native reload log and reload
latency were not captured. Rule 19's absence is about that exact rejected artifact;
its identical behavior condition can still match through approved rule 18.

## Behavioral model and benign outcomes

| Window(s) | Qualifying model evidence | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Binary before 200, control 203 and after 204 | IF score ~0.1430, not qualifying | Falco-backed incidents; do not call these two-layer agreement |
| Sensitive before 201 | IF score ~0.4736, not qualifying | Falco-backed incident |
| Terminal before 202 | IF score ~0.4907, not qualifying | Falco-backed incident |
| Calibration `benign-2-admin`, incident 199 | IF score ~0.8400, qualifying; effective score 24 | Known-benign anomaly-only false positive; not confirmed, no response |
| Three held-out normal windows | No incident in snapshots; accepted events and closed windows verified | No generated-rule hit; no full-pipeline incident in 3/3 windows |

The approved generated rule had zero native hits in three **later** administration,
config-read and curl windows. Those commands repeat calibration workload families;
they are temporally held-out windows, not independent unseen workloads. This does
not justify a production FPR or improvement claim. Calibration had one incident in
nine windows; later checks had zero in three. Do not pool those small convenience
samples with the historical 200-trial benchmark or tune thresholds to erase incident 199.

## Answers to the research questions

- **RQ1, supported loop closure:** observed once (B1), with incident→confirmation→
  template/backtest→human approval→native re-fire and persisted after timeline.
  No ML-only-to-rule path was exercised or implemented.
- **RQ2, human rejection:** observed once (rule 19), despite a passing 0/36 backtest.
  Reviewer choice prevented that exact candidate being added; positive rule 18 is
  separately approved. Broader pattern suppression is not claimed.
- **RQ3, hybrid contribution/coverage:** none of the three primary before incidents
  had qualifying IF evidence; all had existing Falco detections. There is **no new
  attack coverage demonstrated**. The model contributed a benign false positive
  during calibration. That result is retained rather than reframed as a threat.

## Defensible report paragraph

“In a three-behavior controlled mini-study, one process-pattern candidate completed
confirmation, template generation, a 36-event benign backtest, explicit human approval
and native Falco re-fire, with the after incident preserving both original and learned
rule evidence. Two other generated pattern previews exceeded the existing 5% benign
match-rate threshold and were not submitted. A separate passing candidate was manually
rejected and remained absent from the rules file. Three later normal windows produced
no learned-rule matches or incidents. Existing Falco rules detected all three original
behaviors, so the study supports supervised workflow adaptation, not additional attack
coverage. The calibration phase retained one anomaly-only false positive.”

## Reproduce the backtest review on the VM

This reads saved evidence only; it does not confirm, submit, approve, deploy or retrain:

```bash
cd ~/selfsentry
source .venv/bin/activate
python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, 'rule-synthesis-engine')
from pattern_extractor import extract_pattern
from rule_template_generator import generate_rule
from rule_backtester import backtest_rule
p = Path('state/evaluation/academic-loop-20261015T085928Z')
corpus = [json.loads(l) for l in (p/'benign-calibration.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]
assert hashlib.sha256((p/'benign-calibration.jsonl').read_bytes()).hexdigest() == (
    p/'benign-calibration.sha256').read_text().strip()
for case in ('binary', 'sensitive', 'terminal'):
    incident = json.loads((p/f'{case}-before/incidents.json').read_text())[0]
    candidate = generate_rule(extract_pattern(incident), incident['id'])
    print(case, backtest_rule(candidate, corpus))
PY
```

## Remaining scope

C2 recording is still deferred. Recurring VM/Falco timestamp skew is not permanently
fixed by 17 valid captures. Representative baseline/model validation, independent
live layer comparisons, richer supported extraction, broader fault tests and precise
stage/learning timings remain research limitations. The historical 200-trial results
are unchanged. No SVM default change or production platform expansion is proposed.
